Your question is unrelated to the Thunderbird for Android application and therefore outside the scope of support here.

You should follow google's account recovery options as noted on their support page https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/7682439?hl=en

When you select Try another way, look for any of these options:

  • Google prompt: An old phone or tablet where your Gmail account is still signed in.
  • Recovery phone number: A text message or phone call to your registered number.
  • Recovery email: A code sent to your alternative email address.
  • Google Authenticator: If you previously configured it, the app may still generate codes without internet access.
  • Backup codes: Eight-digit codes you may have downloaded or printed when enabling 2FA.
  • Passkey or security key: Another device or physical key previously registered to your account.

Google explains these alternatives in its 2-Step Verification troubleshooting guide . https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185834?ai1hc=1
